correctness.rationale: The exact unit-lattice Zak multiplier is a geometric-series sum with denominators bounded away from zero. The upper envelope is strictly convex in cos frequency and attained at time zero; the positive lower envelopes follow from reverse triangle inequalities and monotonicity and are approached at time one. The zero equation has one admissible phase for intermediate coefficient and only edge limits at the thresholds. Real-analytic scalar multiplication gives full spectrum with no eigenvalues. The 672 supplementary numerical assertions verify examples but do not replace the proof.
